claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has intrinsically high nanoscale lattice distortion.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has intrinsic chemical heterogeneity.
Lattice distortion and chemical heterogeneity create nanoscale localized stress fields.
The localized stress fields impede or pin dislocation motion.
The localized stress fields promote distributed and dynamic activation of slip systems.
Interactions between the localized stress fields and dislocations promote dynamic strain hardening.
Dynamic strain hardening produces more gradual and extended plastic deformation.
The proposed dislocation-mediated deformation mechanism counteracts crack initiation and propagation.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will absorb more mechanical energy before failure and therefore exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten has a relatively brittle high-temperature response compared with WTaTiVZr.
Post-deformation WTaTiVZr will show more complex dislocation interactions and localized deformation features than pure tungsten.
Temperatures of approximately 1000–1500 °C are relevant to sustained plasma-facing-component service.
Testing in inert atmosphere or vacuum discounts oxidation effects.
The proposed property enhancements may not be observable at much lower temperatures.
The proposed property enhancements may not be observable in oxidizing environments.
Potential secondary phases or nanoscale heterogeneities formed during processing may contribute to the improved ductility and toughness.
The WTaTiVZr and pure-tungsten specimens should be prepared with comparable grain sizes and initial defect densities.
A controlled comparison at 1200 °C and constant strain rate can test the proposed difference between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten.
